hbw_calder.accept_text:
He drills them in open ground where anyone can see, which is arrogance. He won't break and run, which isn't.

I'd rather fight one officer than the hundred farmers he's six months from making. That's the whole of my reasoning and I'd say it to his face.

The Hillsbrad Fields are south-east of this tower, in the middle of the valley. He will be on the drill ground.

hbw_militia.accept_text:
In the fields, and I want you to understand I've thought about this longer than it sounds.

They're farmers with billhooks and a grievance, and the grievance is fair - we are standing in their valley. But they've been measuring my gate for a month, and men who measure a gate are deciding something. I'd rather they decided it with ten fewer.

The Hillsbrad Fields, south-east of this tower. You will see the fences from the road.

tm_two_banks.accept_text:
Walk north from this gate, up to the market bridge in the Mill Yard, and look at both banks before you do anything else. That's the whole errand and it saves me a conversation later.

West side is the old village - inn, forge, chapel, the mill. East side is the Society and their vats. Three bridges join them. There is no fourth, the water is deep the whole way, and the wheel does not care who you were.

arw_through_the_wall.description:
Thoradin's Wall closes the south-east corner of Hillsbrad and it has been a closed thing for as long as anyone at Tarren Mill has been posted here. You can see the gap in it from the mill roof on a clear day.

It is open. Commander Thorne has had that confirmed twice and does not believe either of them, because what is on the far side of a wall nobody has crossed in three years is a question with no safe answer.
arw_through_the_wall.accept_text:
I am not sending a column through a gap I know nothing about. I am sending one person, and one person is you.

Get to the gap, get through it, and keep going until you find whoever is holding the other side. Then come back and tell me whether they are holding it against us.

The Wall is south-east of Tarren Mill, at the far end of the valley, past Durnholde and the ogres' stead.

hbw_worgs.accept_text:
They hunt the verges, so take the crown of the road and make them come out to you. That should do it - I'm not standing here counting for you.

And mark where they've been bedding. A worg that beds within sight of a road has stopped being a wolf. It's become a picket, and pickets get posted by something.

hbw_ram_horns.accept_text:
Horns off the foothill rams and I'll have oil in the lamps by Thursday.

Understand what you're doing for me: I can write to Lordaeron and be answered in April, or I can send you up a hill. The Dark Lady gave us our freedom. Nobody thought to give us a supply line.
hbw_ram_horns.turn_in_text: All of them, and two matched. Signed for and counted twice, which means you're in my ledger now. That's a better place to be than most places in this valley.

hbw_living_soil.accept_text:
Jars of loam from six different fields, kept apart - the difference between them is the entire point, so don't fill all of them from the nearest ditch. I'll know.

And since you're not from here: what does soil smell like where you're from? Not a joke. I've been trying to remember what it's supposed to smell like and I find I can't, and I'd rather ask someone who hasn't had the chance to forget.
hbw_living_soil.turn_in_text:
Living. All of them. Roots, mites, the lot.

You said yours smelled like rain on stone. I'm going to think about that for a while.

hbw_farmhands.accept_text:
The Hillsbrad farmhands, out in the rows. But I don't want the count - I want what's in their hands when they go down.

A billhook is a tool a frightened man picks up. A halberd is a thing somebody made, carried to a field, and put into his hands on purpose. If you find halberds out there, this stopped being a harvest watch before either of us arrived.

hbw_arrows.accept_text:
You've got hands and you've got a bench. Batches of rough shafts and we'll call the ram I owe you square.

I'll tell you what I tell the Marshal: my grandfather took rams off that hill when Alterac still had a king, and nobody's shown me the paper that changed it. They dissolved a whole kingdom up there and never once came down here to say who owns the sheep.

hbw_yeti.accept_text:
Up where the grass goes thin, and go in daylight.

I'll say this plain, because I've been told what you are: they tell me you get back up. If that's true then you can walk a gully I'd not send my own son up, and I'd be a liar if I said that didn't sit strange with me. Take the work anyway. I need the pasture more than I need to be comfortable about it.

hbw_murlocs.accept_text:
Off the shingle, and while you're down there keep half an eye on the water behind them.

They come up the beach facing inland. Every one of them. Whatever they're running from is seaward, and I've been watching that water for three weeks and it has never once looked back at me.
hbw_murlocs.turn_in_text:
Done, and the count's still rising.

That's the answer, and it's the one I didn't want. They aren't taking the strand. They're being pushed onto it.

hbw_drowned.accept_text:
The drowned castaways, along the tideline.

Some will have faces I know. Do it anyway. And when you come back, don't tell me which ones - I've spent a month deciding not to find out and I'd like to keep the decision.

hbw_wasps.turn_in_text: I can get a ladder into the north rows for the first time since spring, which is the best news this orchard has had in a year.

hbe_bandits.accept_text:
Off the eastern roads. Violet sashes, and nothing they carry has a maker's mark on it - they file them off, every piece.

Take the sashes if you want my thanks in writing. The colour's Alterac's. They've no kingdom to wear it for and they've kept wearing it anyway, which tells you what we're dealing with better than I can.
hbe_bandits.turn_in_text:
All of them, and the bends are clear.

They'll be manned again by the new moon. Somebody is paying wages, and men who draw wages come back.

hbe_worgs.accept_text:
Worg prowlers, in the hedges between the road and the hollow.

They run in threes. That's not a rule of thumb, it's how they're built - one shows itself, one circles, one waits. If you've found one you've found three, and the third is behind you. Count to three before you swing and you'll be fine.
hbe_worgs.turn_in_text:
And you counted before you swung - I could tell from how few of them got round you.

Most people don't. Most people learn on the second worg, if they get one.

hbe_ditch_samples.accept_text:
Samples - and not jars of ditchwater, I can fill those myself. Take them off the worgs that drink there. Whatever is in that water is in their coats and their gut, and a creature that has been drinking it for a month is a better record of it than anything I could dip.

And before you ask: yes, I know what we do here. That's exactly why I want to be certain it isn't us. If it is, I'd rather find it than have a farmer find it.
hbe_ditch_samples.turn_in_text:
Uphill. All of them, and the worst of them a half mile above the vats.

So it isn't us. Which means I have to go and tell the Society that something else is in this water, and they are going to be very disappointed in me for being right.

hbe_gnolls.accept_text:
In the hollow proper. They den in the low wet ground, so go in from the high side and let them come up to you.

They left the STAKES. Do you understand what that means? They didn't miss them. They pulled the line, coiled the wire, and left me the bits I'd have to dig out. That's not scavenging.
hbe_gnolls.turn_in_text:
Good.

I've been doing this eleven years and I've never once been mocked by the wildlife. I'd like it on record that I'm handling it well.

hbe_snares.accept_text:
That would do me. They hang them up in the dens, which is insulting but at least it's tidy - you'll find them in bunches rather than scattered.

The wire's the thing. I can cut new stakes in an afternoon. Good wire comes up from Southshore twice a year if the road's open, and the road has not been open.
hbe_snares.turn_in_text:
All of them, and six still true. Better than I'd let myself hope for.

The wire alone is a season's work. I'll have a line in the ground by the week's end.

hbe_shamans.accept_text:
You'll hear the rattles long before you see them - and so will everything else in the hollow, so once you start, don't stop to think about it.

A year ago they were dogs with knives. Something has taught them, and taught them quickly, and I would dearly like to know what a gnoll pack had to trade for lessons.
hbe_shamans.turn_in_text:
All of them, and the hollow's drier today than it was yesterday.

I'm not saying that proves anything. I'm saying I've lived here eleven years and I noticed.

hbe_spellbinders.accept_text:
They hold the inner ring and they bind you in place before they do anything else, so go in fast and go in with someone.

Think about the cost of this. A trained binder could sell his talent in any city still standing. Instead he is stood in a scrap camp in the Hillsbrad hills. Somebody is paying him enough to make that the better offer.
hbe_spellbinders.turn_in_text:
Done, and that's the report: somebody in Alterac is funding wizards for a camp that fences stolen cutlery.

That's not a gang any more. That's a government with no country.

hbe_ogres.accept_text:
Round da stead. Dey are slow and dey hit like a wall coming down, so keep moving and never let dem put you against da fences.

I have no love for human farms. But dey built dat barn in a season and da ogres are using it as a privy, and dere is a difference between taking a ting and ruining it.
hbe_ogres.turn_in_text:
Done, and dey are still in da barn.

But dere is more room in it now, and dey have started arguing about who sleeps where. Dat is how dis ends - not wit us.

hbe_riflemen.accept_text:
Along the south road.

Here's the trick, and it cost me a hat to learn it: they sight for the length of the road and not one pace further. Get inside that and a rifle is an expensive club. The danger is the hundred yards before you're inside it.
hbe_riflemen.turn_in_text:
All of them, and I got a measuring chain out on that road this morning for the first time since I was posted here.

That's the whole of what I wanted. The fort can wait; the chain couldn't.

hbe_durnholde_watch.accept_text:
On the bluff outside the walls. And scratch the paint on one before you come back.

Grey underneath. Every single one. They haven't forged a breastplate in fifteen years - they're wearing a dead kingdom's kit with a dead kingdom's colours brushed over it, and they've been doing it so long the paint has worn through at the shoulders.

tm_miller_bands.accept_text:
Bars of iron, smelted proper. Not bronze - I know what bronze does in a wet bearing and so will you after one winter.

Sixty years that wheel's turned. My grandfather kept it going through the Second War by swapping the bands out himself. I'd not like to be the Reed who let it stop over four bars of iron.
tm_miller_bands.turn_in_text:
All of them, and good ones.

She'll turn another sixty on these. I'll not be here for it, but she will, and that's the arrangement we've always had.

tm_innkeeper_pot.accept_text:
Good haunches off the foothill rams, west past the Foothills. Ram, mind, not sheep - there's a difference and this room will tell me about it for a week.

And take the west road, not the hollow. I've lost two suppliers to that hollow and I'd rather keep the one who can carry six.
tm_innkeeper_pot.turn_in_text:
All of them, and hung properly. You've done this before.

Room's yours tonight and I'll not ask which bank you'd rather drink on. Nobody asks that in my house.

tm_smith_charcoal.accept_text:
Oakheart planks, cut and seasoned at a sawmill. I'll burn my own charcoal from them - it's the only way I'll know what went into it.

They keep sending me coal from Dun Garok's old workings. Cheaper, hotter, and it ruins a weld - you get a seam that looks perfect and opens in a year. I'll not put my mark on that for anybody's convenience.

tm_bowyer_yew.accept_text:
The gnolls have been felling the river stand for den stakes. Staves back off them - and look at the cut before you pick one up. Heartwood and sapwood both, or it's firewood and I'll say so.

My father cut there, and his father. There's a mark on one of those trunks that's four generations of us deep. They're burning it to hold up a roof made of my snare wire.
tm_bowyer_yew.turn_in_text:
All of them true, and every one of them off the right side of the trunk.

Four generations of doing it one way, and a gnoll nearly ended it for kindling. I'll string the first tonight.

tm_apprentice_jars.accept_text:
Unmarked jars went out with the Naze consignment before anyone noticed. I need them back, and I need them back closed.

I'm aware how this sounds. But the whole discipline is that you know what you're holding. An unlabelled jar in a Syndicate camp is somebody's accident waiting to be somebody else's epidemic.
tm_apprentice_jars.turn_in_text:
All closed, none of them opened.

You've no idea what a good day this is. I'll have them catalogued by morning and nobody will ever know they left.

tm_chaplain.accept_text:
Markers went missing out of the yard - stone ones, with names cut in them. Syndicate, most likely; cut stone sells.

I'll say the thing nobody here says to you. You die and you get up again, and the people in my yard do not. I've no quarrel with you for it. But you'll understand why a man in my trade thinks about it when you walk past.
tm_chaplain.turn_in_text:
Names back in the ground where they were put.

That's all a marker is - a promise that somebody stays where they were laid. It's the only promise I've got left to keep and I'd rather keep it.

tm_apothecary_reagents.accept_text:
Bloodcaps, out of the wet ground in Mudsnout Hollow. They grow where the water sits.

Cut them, don't pull them - the whole value is in the stem and you'll crush it if you're rough. And don't eat one on a dare. I've had that conversation twice and one of those people is still here, after a fashion.
tm_apothecary_reagents.turn_in_text:
Cut clean. That's a quarter's work secured and one fewer letter I have to write.

Mind the vats on your way out. What's in them isn't finished and it doesn't like being looked at.

tm_vat_tender.turn_in_text:
The cart can go out again.

You'll not understand what that's worth. I was a cooper before. I'm a vat-tender now. It's near enough the same job and it's the only thing that is.
tm_vat_tender.accept_text:
Their binders, inside the keep.

The Society used to send a cart to the undercroft twice a year and nobody minded. Now there are wizards on the gate. Twelve years dead and I've got a trade again - stir it, skim it, log it - and I'm not losing it because Alterac's leftovers found religion.

tm_stable_worgs.accept_text:
Out of the hedges east of the race. Then I'll try the bridge at dusk again and we'll see.

Horses are clever animals and they're not clever in the way people think. They don't reason it out. They just know, and they're right more often than the men leading them.

tm_farrier.accept_text:
Sets of heavy bronze at the forge, and I'll cut the shoe stock off them myself - the plate's the right thickness and the Society's bar stock isn't.

I know it's a strange way round. I'd rather ruin good plate than put another cart team lame on the west road.

tm_commander_syndicate.turn_in_text: They'll replace them. That's the thing about a court - there's always another son. But it buys me a season, and a season in this valley is a long time.
tm_commander_syndicate.accept_text:
Their binders, wherever you find them east of the mill.

Understand what they are. Alterac let the Horde through the pass in the Second War and the Alliance dissolved the kingdom for it. The lords went into these hills with their titles and no land. They are not bandits. They're a court in exile, and courts in exile want their country back.

hbe_route_card.turn_in_text:
Tallies, six hands, one ledger - and not one of those hands is Syndicate.

They were counting for somebody else. I do this work for a living and I did not know anyone else was doing it on my road.

arw_what_killed_the_scout.accept_text:
Four punctures in an arc, and the arc is wider than a wolf's. Whatever did this is standing on that moor right now being perfectly ordinary to everyone who lives there.

Bring me the dewclaws. That will do - I want to see whether the spacing is consistent or whether I am looking at one very large individual.

The moor people call them fleshrippers. Highland fleshrippers, up past the wall.

hbe_fissure_north.accept_text:
The Syndicate off the north track first - they have been sitting on that road watching the elves come and go and taking a tithe, and I would like the road clear before I send anybody up it.

Then go up to the mouth itself and look down it. Do not go in. I have had two men offer and I have told both of them no, and I will tell you the same until somebody can tell me what is at the bottom.

hbw_southshore_watch.turn_in_text:
How many hulls?.. That many.

Then we aren't taking Southshore this year, nor next. I'll send that north and someone in the Undercity will be disappointed in a way that doesn't reach us. Good.

hbe_grik.turn_in_text:
How many?.. Say it once more and then we'll neither of us repeat it.

I'll enter it in the ledger and I'll make sure the ledger is somewhere the farm families never find it.
